solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Resist awkward member of the family

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of the word before it are put in a clumsy new order

explanation.surface: A stubborn relative who won't cooperate with the rest of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sibling is a member of one's own family.

clue.text: Workplace in American institute, insecure on the outside

indicators.note: the word for insecure sits on the outside, wrapping round the institute

parts.note: insecure, lacking confidence, means shy
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone working at an American college feels unsure of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here; the container signal is 'on the outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's forge is the workplace where metal is worked.

clue.text: Course for which one must bring in black dishes

indicators.note: the course must take another letter inside itself

parts.note: a course of study is set out in a syllabus
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A diner on a course is told to fetch dark-coloured plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a meal course; it is a course of study. 'must bring in' puts B inside SYLLABUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabubs are frothy cream desserts, so they are dishes served at the table.

clue.text: Punctilious editor required

parts.note: punctilious, precise in detail, means exact

explanation.surface: A fussy, precise editor was demanded by the publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to demand or require it, so exacted is a past-tense synonym of required.

clue.text: Seeming to be a quiet dad maybe

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a dad is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: A father who appears to be a calm sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent describes how something looks on the surface, which is what seeming means as an adjective.

clue.text: Steak and beer brought to the Lords?

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
the House of Lords is the upper chamber of the UK Parliament, often simply called the House

explanation.surface: A peer is served steak and beer in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A porterhouse is a thick cut of beef steak taken from the loin.

clue.text: Draw a large area of land for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience gets is the sound of the words, so these pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: a tract is a large area of land, so these words say A TRACT

explanation.surface: Sketch an expanse of land for spectators to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Escape from senior member right away outside university

indicators.note: the shortened word stands outside, around the letter for university
right away tells us the letter for right is removed

parts.note: an elder is a senior member of a church or community

explanation.surface: A senior fellow flees his college with no right to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from ELDER, leaving ELDE; 'outside' wraps that around U.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude someone is to escape from or evade them.

clue.text: Modish types upsetting resident

indicators.note: upsetting the word overturns its letter order into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fashionable incomers annoy a long-term local.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendies is an informal word for people who follow the latest fashions, modish types.

clue.text: Bad influence? Couldn't agree more!

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
having a say is having influence

explanation.surface: Someone responding to talk of a corrupting influence with hearty agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an emphatic expression of agreement, the same as couldn't agree more.

clue.text: Push out rubbish for moralist to consume

indicators.note: the moralist eats up the other piece, which ends up inside

parts.note: a prude is a priggish moralist
rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: Putting out the trash for a strait-laced person to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick or push out beyond a surface.

clue.text: Listen to army fighter in South America suffering

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
Che Guevara was a guerrilla fighter in South America

explanation.surface: Tales of an army guerrilla in South America who is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional suffering or anguish.

clue.text: Things that are sure to bring particular obligations

parts.note: certain means particular, as in a certain person
ties are bonds or obligations

explanation.surface: Sure things that come with specific duties attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring' is a link joining the definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Certainties are things that are sure to happen or be true.

clue.text: A body part in the van

parts.note: the head is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A severed body part found inside a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' here is the vanguard, the front, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the van is to be at the forefront, leading the way.

clue.text: Secret lad, he, involved with brunette

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A clandestine affair between a young man and a dark-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' signals an anagram of LAD, HE and BRUNETTE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done secretly or illicitly is done in a hidden, covert way, as an idiom.

clue.text: Polluted bar seemed horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests a messed-up, distorted version of the letters

explanation.surface: A dirty pub looked dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' signals an anagram of BAR and SEEMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Besmeared means smeared over or dirtied, so it is a synonym of polluted.

clue.text: Magnificent object in second place I had

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an end is an object or aim
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Something grand that once came second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in second place' tells you END comes after the letters for 'second' and 'place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid and magnificent both mean impressively grand or excellent.

clue.text: Students troubled as tutor gasped

indicators.note: troubled suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Advanced learners worried when their teacher drew breath in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' signals an anagram of AS, TUTOR and GASPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Postgraduates are students pursuing study after a first degree.

clue.text: Good little creatures shine

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals born together

explanation.surface: Fine young animals with glossy coats.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to shine with sparkling light.

clue.text: First female to get into this bunch of crooks

indicators.note: the first female enters the word this, going inside it

parts.note: in the Bible Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: A woman leading the way to join a gang of criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First female' looks like the start of 'female'; it is the Biblical first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are criminals who steal, so a group of them is a bunch of crooks.

clue.text: Snake outside shelter unaware of what's going on

indicators.note: the snake lies outside, wrapped around the shelter

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A snake curled outside someone's refuge without them noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: A lee is the side of something sheltered from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is oblivious to events around them, so the word means unaware of what's going on.

clue.text: Boredom in kindergarten — nuisance!

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A tiresome child at nursery school causes weariness.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across kindergarTEN NUIsance... the letters EN NUI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing for listless weariness or boredom.

clue.text: They're seen in churches, and they sound like wicked chaps

indicators.note: says that what follows is a word heard, not written

parts.note: knaves are dishonest or wicked men

explanation.surface: Rogues spotted in places of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of KNAVES is silent, so the two words are heard the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A nave is the central body of a church, so naves are found in churches.

clue.text: Poverty seen around — has a meal to be brought in?

indicators.note: the meal-taking word is brought inside the turned word
around turns the word seen back to front

parts.note: to dine is to have a meal, so dines means has a meal

explanation.surface: Destitution seen all around: is anyone bringing food in?
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes NEES; the dash and question mark are just surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is the state of being in want, which is a synonym of poverty.

clue.text: Party with very little Ecstasy? Then end getting joint

parts.note: a do is a party
V is the little, abbreviated form of very
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A party with barely any drugs, ending with someone smoking a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like cannabis in the surface but is the woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking joint used in carpentry.

clue.text: A bit of the Bible making one hostile

parts.note: the Bible is divided into chapters and verses

explanation.surface: A scripture passage that turns someone antagonistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed to it, so it is a synonym of hostile.

clue.text: Daughter is wanting long hair, the pain!

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A girl lacking long locks complains of the anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like 'lacking' but here is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is mental or physical suffering, a synonym of pain.

clue.text: Exhausted, being employed at university

parts.note: used means employed, put to use
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A worn-out student working while still at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Used up means completely worn out or spent, the same as exhausted.
